clue.text: Want rider sending spades back for port worker

parts.note: to want something is to long for it

indicators.note: sending, with back, says the spades letter is sent from inside the rider word
back, with sending, says the spades letter goes back to the start of the rider word

parts.note: a rider on a horse is a horseman
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A docker who wants a horse rider to send spades back, as if gardening tools were being returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spades' looks like garden tools but is the card suit; 'sending back' shifts its letter to the front of the rider. Longshoreman is chiefly American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A longshoreman is the American term for a docker who loads and unloads ships in harbour.

clue.text: Alkaline substances holding up attempt to make porcelain

indicators.note: holding says the alkaline word contains the reversed attempt

parts.note: limes are forms of quicklime, an alkaline substance

indicators.note: in a down answer, up says the attempt word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Chemicals propping up an effort to produce fine china.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' signals reading the attempt word bottom to top; 'holding' makes the chemicals the container. 'to make' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a French city famous for its fine hard-paste china, which bears its name.

clue.text: Mistress Gwynne about to be announced for sport

indicators.note: about says the mistress's name goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: Nell Gwynne was a mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A royal mistress is about to be revealed as a sportswoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be announced' reads as one phrase but splits: 'about' is the container signal and 'to be announced' is TBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team game in which players score by throwing a ball through a high ring.

clue.text: Teams take action about one minor concern

indicators.note: about says the teams word goes round the numeral

parts.note: sides are teams
I is the Roman numeral for one
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Teams going to court over something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a secondary matter, peripheral to the main point being argued.

clue.text: Passing remarks around Republican circle

indicators.note: around says the remarks word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: an obit, or obituary, is remarks made on someone's passing

explanation.surface: Casual comments circulating about a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing remarks' suggests chance comments but means words on a death.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the curved path of a body round a planet or star, a circle.

clue.text: Specimen from partner that was large

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means large

explanation.surface: A sample taken from a former partner who used to be big.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a typical instance or sample of a class, much as a specimen is.

clue.text: Hat manufactured only in Shannon town

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
lone means only, sole

explanation.surface: A hat made only in a town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shannon is Ireland's longest river; Athlone stands on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Athlone is a town in the Irish midlands on the River Shannon.

clue.text: Travelling to stars: reduced pressure in this place?

definitions.text: Travelling to stars: reduced pressure in this place?

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters move about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
P, the abbreviation for pressure, is the word cut down to a letter
here means in this place

explanation.surface: A journey towards the stars, through thin air at altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' shortens pressure to P, and also describes the thin air up there, so the whole clue defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratosphere is the upper atmospheric layer one passes heading for space, where air pressure is low.

clue.text: Rock and roller after work briefly proved alluring

indicators.note: the rocker comes after the work in the answer

parts.note: to temp is to work in short-term jobs
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s rock and roll fan

explanation.surface: A rock and roll musician appeared after a short shift and turned out to be tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a British youth of the 1950s, known for Edwardian-style suits and rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tempted a person drew them in, so it proved attractive or enticing to them.

clue.text: Endure endlessly monstrous and uncomfortable embrace

parts.note: to bear something is to endure it

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for monstrous is cut off

parts.note: monstrous means huge, enormous

explanation.surface: Putting up with a monstrously big, awkward hug.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear hug is a tight, crushing clasp of the arms that can squeeze the breath out of someone.

clue.text: Good angle to enclose ancient stadium where there's no privacy

indicators.note: to enclose says the good and angle letters go round the ancient word

parts.note: to angle is to fish
old means ancient
a bowl is a stadium, like the Hollywood Bowl

explanation.surface: A fine viewpoint enclosing an old arena open to every eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldfish bowl figuratively describes a place or situation in which one is constantly watched.

clue.text: Hound upstanding character for money

parts.note: the Afghan is a breed of hound
the letter I stands upright, a single vertical stroke

explanation.surface: Hounding a person of upright character for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' reads as a verb, to pester, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The afghani is the currency unit of Afghanistan, so it names a kind of money.

clue.text: Looking back, notice painting showing cover on bed

indicators.note: looking back says the word for notice is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to spot something is to notice it
an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: In hindsight, someone spots a painting that shows a bedspread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a garden flower bed, not a bed to sleep in.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsoil is the upper layer of earth that covers a garden bed.

clue.text: In Yorkshire river and lake one sees bird

parts.note: the Ouse is a river flowing through York
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone at a Yorkshire river and lake spots a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse runs through York in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is an old name for the blackbird and the related ring ouzel.

clue.text: Firm, beset by safe crackers, not hearing a thing

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the firm word sits inside the scrambled letters
crackers means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
toned muscles are firm

explanation.surface: A company under attack from safe-crackers, who hear nothing as they work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe crackers' reads as burglars, but 'crackers' (crazy) is the anagram signal for safe, and 'beset by' surrounds the firm word with the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stone-deaf is to be completely deaf, unable to hear any sound at all.

clue.text: Attribute evident when one has a certain something?

definitions.text: Attribute evident when one has a certain something?

parts.words: Attribute evident when one has a certain something?
parts.note: the quality shown by having something is having title to it; a certain something sounds like charisma

explanation.surface: Describing the charm of someone who has that certain something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a certain something' suggests star quality, but read literally it is any particular thing one possesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of possessing a thing, evident whenever someone has a particular item.

clue.text: Vegetarian food and beer with no head?

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
O, the figure zero, means none
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A meat-free meal plus a beer without its frothy top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no head' looks like a flat pint, but 'no' is O and 'head' is BEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The pinto bean is a mottled kidney bean, a staple of meat-free cooking.

clue.text: Dangerous person overturning barrel and wine box

indicators.note: overturning in a down answer turns the barrel word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer
a case is a box of wine bottles

explanation.surface: A menace knocks over a barrel and a crate of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is an informal word for a crazy and possibly dangerous person.

clue.text: Work with uranium, fast becoming rich

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Working with uranium, quickly growing wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like quickly but is a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy or lavish, showing great riches.

clue.text: Composer hit with bottle

definitions.meaning: Philip ... is an American minimalist composer
to ... someone is to attack them with a ... or bottle

explanation.surface: A composer struck with a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Glass wrote minimalist operas, and glassing someone is British slang for an assault with drinking vessels.

clue.text: Leave university over a revolutionary painting technique

parts.note: to go is to leave
Che Guevara was a Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Dropping out of college over a rebel art method.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouache is painting in opaque watercolour bound with gum, a distinct method of painting.

clue.text: Gathered together as dames dancing around

indicators.note: dancing around suggests the letters move about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ladies dancing in a ring, gathered together.
explanation.definitionFit: Amassed means collected or accumulated, brought together in quantity.

clue.text: Turn over as e-books deteriorate

parts.note: taken as written
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
to rust is to decay or deteriorate

explanation.surface: Handing things over as electronic books decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrust something is to hand it over to another's care, as in turning over responsibility.

clue.text: Leitmotiv Keith Emerson embodies

indicators.note: embodies says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The rock keyboardist Keith Emerson personifies a recurring musical idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a recurring musical phrase tied to a character or idea, a kind of theme.

clue.text: Unscripted talk in theatre stems from garden

definitions.meaning: the word actors mutter to make background crowd noise
a plant grown for its edible stalks

explanation.surface: Ad-libbed chat on stage about produce from the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras repeat the word to imitate crowd murmur, and the plant's pink stalks are cooked as fruit.

clue.text: Stand before entrance doing twirl

indicators.note: doing a twirl turns the entrance word round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone stands in front of a doorway, twirling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a verb but is a noun, a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An etagere is a set of open shelves for displaying ornaments, a kind of display stand.

clue.text: Cutting article from writer seen as mediocre and dated

parts.note: a hack is a writer of dull, routine work
to have seen someone is to have dated them, so saw means dated

explanation.surface: A newspaper cutting by a second-rate writer, judged mediocre and old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting article' suggests a press cutting, but it is a cutting tool; 'dated' means went out with, not old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a tool with a fine-toothed blade for sawing through metal.

clue.text: What might provide recent magazine feature?

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: its first word scattered about yields the clue word recent

explanation.surface: Asking what would supply the latest issue's feature article.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: spread the letters of CENTRE about and they make RECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre spread is the pair of facing pages in the middle of a magazine, often used for a big feature.
